processingFeeNote: Up to 1.50% of the loan amount + GST, minimum ₹1,000 and maximum ₹15,000. 100% waiver for Defence and Platinum/Rhodium salary-package customers; 50% waiver for Government employees and for a CIC score of 800 or above.
notes: Rate published as 2-year MCLR 8.75% plus a 1.25%–6.25% spread, effective 10.00%–15.00% p.a. as on 01.04.2026. Salaried only, and only for customers holding an SBI salary package account. SBI publishes an EMI/NMI ceiling of 65% rather than a minimum CIBIL score. SBI's pages are rendered client-side, so the eligibility tabs (minimum salary, tenure band, document list) could not be read by the crawler this run and are left null rather than guessed.

processingFeeNote: Up to ₹6,500 + GST, non-refundable even if the loan is later cancelled or rebooked.
prepaymentCharges: Foreclosure on principal outstanding: 4% up to 24 EMIs, 3% after 24 and up to 36 EMIs, 2% after 36 EMIs. Part-payment allowed after the first EMI, up to 25% of principal outstanding, once a financial year and twice in the loan tenure, at the same percentages.
notes: Rack rate for salaried applicants is published as 9.99%–24.00%; HDFC also publishes actual Q1 FY2026-27 disbursals of 9.97%–24.06% IRR (average 10.89%). Loans up to ₹50 lakh, and up to ₹75 lakh subject to eligibility norms. Self-employed applicants are explicitly not eligible for this product. No minimum CIBIL is published as a rule — the FAQ calls a score above 720 'ideal', so no floor is stored. Under the Golden Edge programme foreclosure is free after 12 EMIs for customers with income ≥ ₹75,000 and a loan above ₹15 lakh.

prepaymentCharges: 3% of the outstanding principal amount; nil after 24 EMIs have been paid.
notes: Rate is published as 1-year MCLR 8.40% plus a 1.59%–8.10% spread, effective 9.99%–16.50% p.a., with a published April–June 2026 mean of 11.45%. ICICI's product and eligibility pages are rendered client-side and publish no loan amount band, tenure band, minimum salary or minimum CIBIL in crawlable text, so those fields are left null.

processingFeeNote: Up to 2% of the loan amount + GST.
prepaymentCharges: Foreclosure on principal outstanding — disbursed amount below ₹10 lakh: 3% up to 36 paid EMIs, 2% after. ₹10 lakh and above from own funds: 3% before 12 paid EMIs, nil after. Part payment: 3% up to 36 paid EMIs, 2% after; up to 25% of principal outstanding a year is free after 12 paid EMIs.
notes: Axis publishes the product as fixed-rate 3-year MCLR 8.90% plus a 0%–12.65% spread, effective 8.90%–21.55% p.a. with no reset; the same page reports actual April–June 2026 disbursals of 8.75%–21.55% (mean 13.07%), while the headline banner advertises 'starting at 9.99%'. The wider published MCLR band is stored. No minimum salary or CIBIL score is published on either page.

processingFeeNote: Up to 5% of the final loan amount plus taxes, non-refundable, deducted at disbursal.
prepaymentCharges: Foreclosure and part payment: 4% + taxes up to 3 years, 2% + taxes after 3 years, on the outstanding principal or part-payment amount. No lock-in after the first EMI; part payment is allowed once a financial year up to 20% of principal outstanding.
notes: Kotak publishes a fixed rate 'starting from 10.99% p.a.' and no ceiling, so no maximum is stored. Loans up to ₹1 crore for 1–6 years. Minimum net monthly income is published per segment: ₹25,000 for Kotak salary-account holders, ₹30,000 otherwise and ₹20,000 for Kotak employees — the ₹25,000 figure is stored. The eligibility page calls a CIBIL score of 750 'generally considered good' rather than a floor, so no minimum score is stored.

processingFeeNote: Up to 4.13% of the loan amount (inclusive of applicable taxes); Flexi loans carry a separate fee of ₹1,999 to ₹18,999.
prepaymentCharges: Term loan and Flexi Dropline/Hybrid: up to 4.72% (inclusive of taxes) of the outstanding loan amount on full pre-payment, and of the amount prepaid on part pre-payment. Flexi loans carry no part-prepayment charge.
documents: KYC document (Aadhaar / passport / voter ID / driving licence)
notes: Rate of interest published as a full range of 10% to 30.5% p.a. CIBIL 650 is published as an eligibility criterion, not a preference, so it is stored as a floor. The published age band runs to 80 years, with the borrower required to be 80 or younger at the end of the tenure. No minimum salary is published.

PNB Sahyog Rin (personal loan scheme for public) floating rates run from RLLR+BSP+2.15% (presently 10.25%) for Defence and paramilitary salary-account holders to RLLR+BSP+7.70% (presently 15.80%) for check-off borrowers scoring under 681; fixed-rate options are 1% higher. Quantum is up to 24 times gross monthly salary capped at ₹20 lakh, repayable within the remaining service period or 72 EMIs, whichever is earlier. Rates are tiered by CIBIL band down to 'below 681', so there is no published cut-off score. Prepayment carries no penalty.

processingFeeNote: 0.50% of the loan amount, minimum ₹1,000 and maximum ₹5,000 (+ GST); 50% waived during the Retail Loan Festival from 01.07.2026 to 30.09.2026.
notes: Canara Budget is the bank's personal loan for confirmed salaried employees: 9.70%–14.70% on contracted loans w.e.f. 12.12.2025, published mean 11.86%. Quantum is 25 months' gross salary, capped at ₹50 lakh under Canara Budget Prime (government, defence, PSU) and ₹40 lakh under Canara Budget Delight (corporates and institutions) — the higher cap is stored. Repayable in up to 84 EMIs. Instead of a salary floor the bank publishes a net-take-home rule: at least 25% of gross salary or ₹10,000 a month, whichever is higher, after all instalments.

processingFeeNote: Up to 3.5% of the loan amount plus documentation charges, deducted at disbursal.
notes: Rates start at 10.49% p.a. with no published ceiling. Instant personal loans run from ₹30,000 to ₹5 lakh over 12–48 months; above ₹5 lakh the bank lends up to ₹50 lakh for up to 84 months with fuller documentation. The FAQ states a minimum CIBIL score of 730 is required, so it is stored as a floor. Salaried applicants need ₹25,000 net monthly income; self-employed applicants are assessed on age 25–65 and annual net income of at least ₹4.8 lakh, and no salaried age band is published.

processingFeeNote: Up to 2.5% of the loan proceeds.
notes: Yes Bank publishes a full 10.85%–21% p.a. range and processing charges of up to 2.5%, plus stamp duty as per state law. The product page itself renders no crawlable content, so loan amount, tenure, minimum income, age and CIBIL criteria are not stored — the bank does not publish them in readable text on the pages scraped.

processingFeeNote: 2% on FIRSTmoney (from 0% on select loan amounts), against up to 4% on traditional personal loans.
prepaymentCharges: Zero foreclosure and zero prepayment charges
notes: FIRSTmoney Smart Personal Loan: ₹50,000 to ₹15 lakh, 9 to 60 months, rates from 9.99% p.a. on a reducing balance with no published ceiling, and explicitly zero foreclosure or prepayment charges. The bank states the applicant's CIBIL score should be 710 or more, so it is stored as a floor, and publishes a ₹25,000 minimum monthly salary.

prepaymentCharges: Prepayment allowed in part or in full; the charge is not published on the personal loan pages.
notes: Federal Bank's two official pages disagree on the floor: the rate-card page publishes 'Personal Loan — onwards 11.99%', while the FedPremia FAQ publishes a range of 10.49% to 17.99% p.a. The higher, more conservative floor and the published ceiling are stored together. FedPremia is for salaried applicants earning at least ₹25,000 a month, with a maximum tenure of 60 months.

processingFeeNote: 2% of the loan value, deducted at disbursement.
prepaymentCharges: 5% of the outstanding principal if foreclosed within the first 18 EMIs, 3% after 18 EMIs. Nil if at least 12 EMIs have been paid without a bounce and the closure is from own funds — a balance transfer does not count as own funds.
notes: RBL publishes a single flat rate of 18% p.a. rather than a range. The offer is limited to existing customers holding a salary or savings account, from ₹30,000 to ₹5 lakh over 12–36 months, with the borrower aged 25 to 55 at onboarding. No minimum salary or CIBIL score is published.

processingFeeNote: Up to 5% of the loan amount + GST on the product page; the rates page shows up to 3% + GST for some profiles, plus documentation charges of up to ₹1,000 + GST.
prepaymentCharges: Part prepayment of up to 25% of the disbursed amount is free at any time. Beyond that: 6.5% of the amount prepaid within 12 months of first disbursement, 4.5% after. Foreclosure: 6.5% of principal outstanding within 12 months, 4.5% after. Zero on floating-rate loans to individuals.
notes: Published range is 10.99% to 29.99% p.a. Salaried applicants: age 21–58, minimum monthly income ₹15,000 (₹25,000 in metros). Self-employed: age 25–65, minimum annual income ₹3 lakh and three years of business vintage. Tata Capital's wording on credit score is inconsistent — the product page says loans go to individuals 'with a credit score of 725 and above' while the eligibility list says '725+ preferred' — so no hard floor is stored.

processingFeeNote: Up to 4% of the loan amount, deducted upfront before disbursement.
prepaymentCharges: Foreclosure charges apply; L&T Finance publishes that the exact percentage is set in the individual loan agreement.
notes: The rate page headline reads 'starting @11%' but the published rate table on the same page gives a minimum interest rate of 10.50% and states the maximum is 'as applicable to your profile' — the table figure is stored and no ceiling is recorded. Loans up to ₹30 lakh. No minimum salary, age band, tenure band or CIBIL floor is published.

Muthoot publishes interest rates 'starting at just 13.5% p.a.' with no ceiling, personal loans up to ₹20 lakh and a maximum tenure of five years, and an age band of 21 to 60. It states only that a 'good credit score' is assessed and that processing charges are 'decided from time to time', so no CIBIL floor and no processing fee are stored.

processingFeeNote: Up to 4% of the loan sanctioned amount.
prepaymentCharges: Part-prepayment: up to 7% of the amount prepaid within 13 months of disbursal, up to 6% between 13 and 25 months, up to 5% after 25 months, with up to 20% of principal outstanding a year permitted. Foreclosure follows the same 7% / 6% / 5% schedule on principal outstanding. Fixed-rate loans only.
documents: Identity proof (Aadhaar / PAN / passport / voter ID)
Address proof (utility bill, Aadhaar, passport or rental agreement)
Bank statements - last 6 months showing salary credits
notes: The published indicative range of rate of interest is 10% to 28% p.a. Loans up to ₹50 lakh for 1 to 7 years, for salaried employees aged 21 to 60. A CIBIL score of 750 or more is described as helping quicker approval and better terms rather than as a cut-off, so no floor is stored. No minimum salary is published.

processingFeeNote: Up to 5% of the loan amount.
prepaymentCharges: Up to 4% foreclosure charge, with no foreclosure permitted within 12 months of the first EMI. An additional 2% applies if the loan is transferred to another financial institution.
documents: KYC documents (Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID)
Address proof (utility bill, rental agreement or passport)
Cancelled cheque and eNACH mandate form
notes: Shriram publishes rates 'starting at 11% p.a.' with no ceiling, loans up to ₹10 lakh over 12 to 60 months, and an age band of 21 at application to 60 at loan closure. Self-employed applicants qualify only as pre-approved customers with an existing Shriram relationship, or are directed to a business loan instead. No minimum salary or CIBIL score is published.

processingFeeNote: Published as up to 4% plus applicable taxes in the rate table; the feature summary on the same page quotes a 0%–3% band.
prepaymentCharges: Before the first 6 EMIs: 4% of the amount prepaid + taxes, including balance transfer. After 6 EMIs: nil from the borrower's own funds, 4% from other sources including a balance transfer.
notes: Published rate is '9.99% p.a. onwards' with no ceiling, for loans of ₹1 lakh to ₹50 lakh over 12 to 84 months, for salaried and self-employed applicants. No minimum salary, age band or CIBIL floor is published on the rate and charges page.

processingFeeNote: Starts from 2.5% of the loan amount + GST.
prepaymentCharges: No prepayment charges. Foreclosure: 5% + GST on the outstanding principal.
notes: Hero FinCorp's rate-card table itself only says 'as per eligibility', but its interest rate calculator and product pages publish a fixed rate starting at 18% p.a. on a reducing balance, so 18% is stored as the floor and no ceiling is recorded. Instant personal loans up to ₹7 lakh (the application journey quotes ₹50,000–₹5 lakh) over 12 to 36 months, minimum monthly income ₹15,000, age 21 to 60. A CIBIL score of 725 or above is described as 'preferred', not required, so no floor is stored.
